evals.prompt: Build an admin users page in the existing Next.js App Router app with URL-backed filters, paginated GraphQL data, loading/error/empty states, and an edit mutation.
evals.expected_output: A project-aligned feature using existing routing, query, form, cache, UI, accessibility, and responsive patterns.
expectations: Inspects and follows the nearest feature structure before adding abstractions
Keeps server state in the established query layer and URL state shareable
Defines loading, error, empty, success, and mutation feedback states
Updates or invalidates cache through the project's established query keys

evals.prompt: Diagnose a hydration mismatch on a dashboard card that formats the current date and reads localStorage during render. Do not implement a fix.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-based diagnosis separating nondeterministic server rendering from browser-only storage access and explaining safe correction options without editing files.
expectations: Identifies server/client date divergence as a hydration risk
Identifies render-time localStorage access as browser-only behavior
Distinguishes diagnosis from implementation
Recommends the smallest compatible boundary or initialization strategy

evals.prompt: Implement a Next.js feature that sends an invitation through GraphQL. The component currently imports the mutation document and declares its TanStack Query mutation key inline.
evals.expected_output: A feature operations module owns the typed GraphQL mutation hook while the component consumes that named hook and retains only UI-specific callbacks.
expectations: Moves the GraphQL document and mutation key into a named derived operation hook
Does not configure the GraphQL document or mutation key directly in the component
Keeps targeted cache updates, pending guards, and UI feedback at the appropriate feature boundary

evals.prompt: Implement a production admin screen from a polished HTML prototype. The prototype stores records in component state, validates required fields with submit-handler if statements, and mutates the local array after a fake delay.
evals.expected_output: A fidelity-preserving implementation that treats prototype runtime code as demonstration only and maps the screen through the repository's real form, GraphQL, TanStack Query, API validation, error, and cache patterns.
expectations: Records a prototype-to-production mapping before implementation
Keeps server records in the established query cache instead of copying the prototype array into local state
Uses react-hook-form plus zod for client feedback and requires independent API validation and authorization
Implements the named query/mutation wrapper and targeted cache update or rollback while preserving the prototype's observable states

evals.prompt: Add an 'Approve' step to the campaign editor: staff generate a draft with an AI route handler, edit it in a form that includes a list of ad objects, then approve it so the next step can use it.
evals.expected_output: The approval is gated on the server, model output is coerced and rebuilt from an allowlist before it is saved as a draft, and the edit form gives every structured field a real editor.
expectations: Enforces the predecessor check in the route handler and returns 409 with a readable message, not only a disabled button
Saves generated output as a draft and never lets model output set the approved state
Rebuilds the saved record from an allowlist of keys instead of spreading the model response
Records a version of every input the next step reads so a re-approved upstream marks the child stale
Gives the list of ad objects an editor with explicit to-text and from-text mapping instead of JSON.stringify

evals.prompt: Product wants the 'Advanced' section of a saved record renamed to 'Delivery settings' in the UI. The record is stored with an `advanced` field and exported as JSON. What should the change include?
evals.expected_output: Treats the request as a copy change: every visible label and message is updated, while the stored `advanced` field and the JSON export key stay as they are; renaming the key is described as a separate data change needing a migration or read fallback.
expectations: Updates every visible place the section is named, including buttons and error messages
Leaves the persisted `advanced` field and the export key unchanged
Explains that renaming the stored key needs a migration or read fallback for existing records
Keeps any stored-key rename out of the label change

evals.prompt: A multi-step onboarding form has a 'Save and finish later' button. Users report that when one box is half-typed (for example an email like `jane@acme`), pressing it saves nothing and they come back to an empty form. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Separates the draft save from the final submit: the draft stores every valid field, leaves the malformed one out, and the form marks the named field; the final submit stays all or nothing, and resuming reads the stored draft back into the form on the saved step.
expectations: Keeps the final submit all or nothing on required fields and format rules
Makes a draft save store the valid fields instead of refusing the whole save over one malformed field
Never stores the malformed value to make the draft succeed
Shows the fields that were not stored with their inline errors and a message saying the save was partial
Resumes from the stored draft, including the step the user stopped on
Adds tests for a draft with one malformed field and for the same input sent as a submit
